DSH guided tour

A video-style, captioned walkthrough with saved interface screenshots and design illustrations.

Overview

1. Welcome to DSH

Work with code, documents and analysis in your browser. Use the manual for the full steps and operator setup.

Sign-in layout

2. Sign in

Enter your DSH account. Leave No Internet / Internal selected. Use the floating User manual button whenever you need help.

Private user→Selected environment→Internal tools + local inference

Environment design

3. Choose your environment

No Internet is the default. Internet needs an administrator grant and uses separate files, history and credentials.

Actual synthetic tool-session capture

4. Start a project

Choose a workspace and working directory. Ask a bounded question, name the files and request source citations.

Private user→Selected environment→Internal tools + local inference

Execution boundaries

5. Verify tools and outputs

Review changes, inspect generated files and open previews through authenticated routes. The terminal runs in your private environment.

Private user→Incoming packages→Approval → offline cache

Dependency transfer

6. Prepare offline packages

Download in Internet, request source/version/hash review, then install from the read-only approved cache in No Internet.

Private user→Selected environment→Internal tools + local inference

Context and concurrency

7. Understand long context

A 1M total budget includes tools and output. Cold preparation takes time; long admission is bounded while ordinary requests remain concurrent.

Private user→Selected environment→Internal tools + local inference

Managed clients

8. Use managed clients

Claude Code, TrueForge and Kilo run inside the selected environment through internal LiteLLM. Their state stays within that environment.

Dashboard illustration — demonstration data

9. Administer access

Use Admin overview to manage provisioned accounts, grant Internet permission and inspect sessions, storage and token summaries.

Private user→Selected environment→Internal tools + local inference

10. Install and operate

Follow the installation chapter in order. LLM/GPU setup is the final technical chapter; accepted stress results are explained separately.
